I recommend trying OpenCode in a different environment, whether on another computer, a virtual machine, or even in a Docker container. This will help you determine if the problem is related to your PC or a specific configuration.

As an alternative, if this doesn’t resolve the issue, consider disabling IPv6. In my experience, when OpenCode wouldn't show the user interface, others encountered blank or black screens as well. Disabling IPv6 was the solution I found. You can do this by running the following command in your terminal:

```bash
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv6.conf.all.disable_ipv6=1
```
This command temporarily disables IPv6.

You can find more information: #11092

We temporarily resolved the problem using the following steps:
1. Install the glibc compatibility layer: Use sgerrand/alpine-pkg-glibc to import the glibc library files into Alpine.
2. Force download of the glibc binary: Manually download opencode-linux-x64.tar.gz (the glibc compiled version) from GitHub Releases instead of using the official installation script (which will automatically detect and install the musl version).


```dockerfile
FROM ghcr.io/anomalyco/opencode:1.2.15

USER root

ENV GLIBC_RELEASE_VERSION=2.35-r1
ENV BUN_VERSION=1.3.9

RUN apk del libc6-compat gcompat || true \
    && apk add --no-cache curl libstdc++ unzip bash \
    && curl -L https://alpine-pkgs.sgerrand.com/sgerrand.rsa.pub -o /etc/apk/keys/sgerrand.rsa.pub \
    && curl -L https://github.com/sgerrand/alpine-pkg-glibc/releases/download/${GLIBC_RELEASE_VERSION}/glibc-${GLIBC_RELEASE_VERSION}.apk -o glibc.apk \
    && apk add --no-cache --force-overwrite glibc.apk \
    && rm glibc.apk

RUN curl -fsSL https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/releases/download/v1.2.15/opencode-linux-x64.tar.gz -o opencode.tar.gz \
    && tar -xzf opencode.tar.gz -C /usr/local/bin \
    && rm opencode.tar.gz \
    && chmod +x /usr/local/bin/opencode \
    # Ensure glibc loader is in the standard path
    && mkdir -p /lib64 \
    && ln -sf /usr/glibc-compat/lib/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2 /lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2

ENV LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/glibc-compat/lib
```


Hopefully this method can help others!
